## Definition

A **scatterplot** is a graph that displays the relationship between two continuous variables, with one variable on the x-axis and the other on the y-axis. Each point represents one observation.

## Purpose

Scatterplots help you:

- Visualise relationships between variables
- Identify the direction of correlation (positive/negative)
- Assess linearity of the relationship
- Detect outliers
- Check assumptions before correlation analysis

## Interpreting Patterns

```
Positive Correlation    Negative Correlation    No Correlation
        ●                        ●                   ●  ●
       ●  ●                       ●  ●             ●     ●
      ●  ●                          ●  ●        ●   ●   ●
     ●  ●                             ●  ●       ● ●  ●
    ●  ●                                ●  ●   ●    ●

Curved (Non-linear)     Outlier Effect
     ●●●●                      ●
   ●●
  ●                       ●●●●●●
 ●                        ●●●●●●
●●●●●                     ●●●●●●
```

## R Code Example

```r
# Basic scatterplot
plot(x, y,
     xlab = "Variable X",
     ylab = "Variable Y",
     main = "Relationship between X and Y")

# With ggplot2
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data, aes(x = variable1, y = variable2)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +  # Add trend line
  labs(x = "Variable 1", y = "Variable 2")

# Check linearity before Pearson's r
plot(x, y)
abline(lm(y ~ x), col = "red")
```

## Adding a Line of Best Fit

The **regression line** summarises the relationship:

```
         ●
        ●╱●
       ╱●
     ●╱●
    ╱●●
   ╱●
  ●

Line of best fit minimises
distance from points to line
```

## What to Look For

| Pattern | Interpretation |
|---------|----------------|
| Upward slope | Positive correlation |
| Downward slope | Negative correlation |
| Tight cluster | Strong correlation |
| Wide scatter | Weak correlation |
| Curve | Non-linear relationship |
| Isolated point | Potential outlier |
